title: Придаточные 3–5: whose, whom, where; дополнительная информация; -ing/-ed clauses
summary: Научимся говорить «у которого», «где», «в тот день, когда», отличать уточнение от «кстати» с запятыми (my brother, who lives in Berlin), строить all of whom и , which surprised everyone — и сжимать придаточные до the guy talking to Tom и the game made by two people.

grammar.title: 1. Главная идея: «какой именно» или «кстати, …»
grammar.html:
Что вы уже знаете (урок B1-21): who / that / which склеивают две фразы, «который» можно выбросить (the game I bought), а предлог уходит в конец (the guy I work with). Теперь главное открытие B2: придаточные бывают двух типов. Первый отвечает на вопрос «какой именно?». Второй просто добавляет информацию — «кстати, …». По-русски запятая стоит всегда, а в английском именно запятая показывает тип.
Русский

Женщина, которая живёт по соседству, — врач.

Мой брат Бен, который живёт в Гонконге, — архитектор.

Обе фразы с запятыми.

English

The woman who lives next door is a doctor. — какая именно? Без запятых.

My brother Ben, who lives in Hong Kong, is an architect. — и так ясно, кто; просто добавка. С запятыми.

Придаточное с запятыми можно вырезать — и фраза не потеряет смысла: My brother Ben is an architect. Первый тип вырезать нельзя: The woman is a doctor — какая женщина?

grammar.title: 2. whose — «чей», «у которого»
grammar.html:
whose заменяет his, her, their, its в придаточном. По-русски это «у которого», «чей», «которого (кого-то)». После whose всегда идёт существительное.
Две фразыОдна фраза
We helped some people. Their car had broken down.We helped some people whose car had broken down.
I follow a streamer. His cat always sits on the keyboard.I follow a streamer whose cat always sits on the keyboard.
I met a girl. I went to school with her brother.I met a girl whose brother I went to school with.

Сравните who и whose:

  • I met a man who knows you. — …который знает тебя. (он знает)
  • I met a man whose sister knows you. — …сестра которого знает тебя. (его сестра знает)

whose можно и для компаний, стран, вещей: It's a studio whose games are all about cats. — Это студия, все игры которой — про котов.

I have a friend who's brother is a pilot.
I have a friend whose brother is a pilot.

who's звучит так же, но это who is / who has: I have a friend who's learning Korean. I have a friend who's just moved to Seoul.

A designer whose his work I love.
A designer whose work I love. — whose уже значит «его»

grammar.title: 3. whom, where, the day, the reason
grammar.html:
whom — «которого, которому» (когда человек — дополнение). Это официально: письма, статьи, новости. В разговоре говорят who или вообще ничего:

ОфициальноВ жизни
a person whom I admirea person I admire
friends with whom you can relaxfriends you can relax with

where — для места, «где, в котором»:

  • I went back to the town where I grew up. — Я вернулся в город, где вырос.
  • The café where we met has closed. — Кафе, где мы познакомились, закрылось.
  • I'd love to live somewhere where it's warm all year.
The city where I visited last year.
The city (that) I visited last year. — visit что? город; «где» тут нет
Проверка: если внутри можно сказать there (I grew up there) — ставьте where. Если там it (I visited it) — that / which или ничего.

the day, the time, the year — обычно без слова: That's the day I'm flying to Oslo. The last time I saw her, she had blue hair. Можно that или when.

the reason — без слова, с that или с why: The reason I'm calling is to ask for your advice. = The reason why I'm calling…

grammar.title: 4. Добавка с запятыми: , who / , which
grammar.html:
У придаточного-«добавки» три жёстких правила — и все три противоположны тому, что вы учили в B1-21.
Какой именноДобавка
запятыенетда
thatможнонельзя
убрать словоможно (если не подлежащее)нельзя
  • John, who speaks four languages, works as a guide. — Джон, который говорит на четырёх языках, работает гидом.
  • Anna told me about her new job, which she's enjoying a lot.
  • We stayed at the Park Hotel, which a friend had recommended.
  • This morning I met Chris, who I hadn't seen for ages. (можно whom)
  • Kate has just been to Sweden, where her daughter lives.
  • Lisa, whose car had broken down, was in a terrible mood.
We played Hades, that I'd recommended to everyone.
We played Hades, which I'd recommended to everyone.

Запятая меняет смысл:

  • My sister who lives in Berlin is a designer. — у меня несколько сестёр, говорю о той, что в Берлине.
  • My sister, who lives in Berlin, is a designer. — сестра одна; «кстати, она в Берлине».

grammar.title: 5. Предлог + whom / which; all of whom, none of which
grammar.html:
В официальном английском предлог встаёт перед whom / which — прямо как в русском «с которым», «без которой». В разговоре предлог уходит в конец, и тогда whom не говорят.
ОфициальноРазговорно
Mr Lee, to whom I spoke yesterday, agreed.Mr Lee, who I spoke to yesterday, agreed.
the studio for which she worksthe studio she works for
  • Luckily we had a map, without which we would have got lost. — …без которой мы бы заблудились.
  • She works for a company called Nimbus, which I'd never heard of.
Mr Lee, to who I spoke, agreed.
Mr Lee, to whom I spoke, agreed. / Mr Lee, who I spoke to, agreed.

Число / часть + of whom (люди) / of which (вещи) — «из которых»:

  • Helen has three brothers, all of whom are married. — …все из которых женаты.
  • They asked me a lot of questions, most of which I couldn't answer.
  • I tried on three jackets, none of which fitted me.
  • Two men, neither of whom I'd seen before, walked into the office.
  • We have four monitors, two of which we never use.
  • We stayed in a lovely hotel, the name of which I've forgotten.
I have ten followers, most of them are bots.
I have ten followers, most of whom are bots. (или: …ten followers. Most of them are bots.)

grammar.title: 6. , which — про всю фразу целиком
grammar.html:
Иногда «что» относится не к одному слову, а к всему событию: «Джо получил работу, что всех удивило». По-английски тут только , which — и никогда не what.
целая фраза,which+комментарий
  • Joe got the job, which surprised everyone. — Джо получил работу, что всех удивило.
  • Sarah couldn't come, which was a shame. — Сара не смогла прийти, и это обидно.
  • The weather was great, which we hadn't expected. — Погода была отличная, чего мы не ожидали.
  • The patch deleted everyone's saves, which made the players furious.
  • He said he'd send the files by Monday, which means Wednesday. — …а это значит, в среду.
The server went down, what was annoying.
The server went down, which was annoying.
В живой речи , which is… — любимый способ добавить свою оценку: …which is fine, …which is crazy, …which is why I left.

grammar.title: 7. the woman talking to Tom, the game made by two people
grammar.html:
Придаточное можно сжать: убираем who is / that was — и остаётся -ing (активный смысл: сам делает) или 3-я форма (пассивный смысл: с ним сделали). В B2-5 -ing относился к действию; здесь он описывает существительное, как русское причастие «разговаривающий», «сделанный».
ПолностьюСжато
the woman who is talking to Tomthe woman talking to Tom
people who were waiting outsidepeople waiting outside
the boy who was injured in the accidentthe boy injured in the accident
a game that was made by two peoplea game made by two people

-ing — и для «прямо сейчас», и для «всегда»:

  • Police investigating the robbery want to talk to you. — Полиция, расследующая ограбление…
  • I was woken up by a dog barking. — Меня разбудил лай собаки.
  • The road connecting the two villages is very narrow. (всегда соединяет)
  • I have a room overlooking the park. — У меня комната с видом на парк.
  • Name a game beginning with Z.

3-я форма — пассивный смысл; помните про неправильные (stolen, made, built, written):

  • The money stolen in the robbery was never found.
  • Most of the phones made in this factory are exported.
  • He showed me some sketches drawn by his grandfather.

С there is / there was: There were some kids swimming in the river. · Is there anybody waiting? · There was a red car parked outside. А left = «оставшийся»: There's only one slice left.

The man was sitting next to me snored all flight.
The man sitting next to me snored all flight. / The man who was sitting…
A game making by two people.
A game made by two people. — игру сделали, она сама не делает

We watched Arcane, which I loved.

She has two cats, both of which sleep all day.

The team won, which nobody expected.

The man I spoke to… / The man to whom I spoke…
The car stealing last night was found.
The car stolen last night was found.
Итог юнита в одной строке
whose + существительное · where = there · запятые = добавка: , who / , which, без that · all of whom / none of which · , which про всю фразу · the guy talking / the game made.

texts.title: The studio in the old bakery
texts.text:
If you've played Lantern Road, which came out last year and sold over a million copies, you probably imagine a big studio with glass walls. In fact, the game was made by seven people working in an old bakery in a small Scottish town called Kelby, where the founder, Maya Ross, grew up.

Maya, whose parents ran the bakery for thirty years, started making games at the age of fourteen. "The first game I made was about a cat delivering bread," she laughs. "Nobody played it except my mum, who still says it's the best game ever made."

After university she worked in London for a big company, the name of which she prefers not to mention. "I learned a lot there, but I was one of four hundred people, most of whom never knew what the others were doing." When her parents retired, she moved back to Kelby and turned the bakery into an office.

The team she hired is small and unusual. There are two artists, both of whom used to work in animation, a programmer who had never made a game before, and a composer whose music you may have heard in a popular TV series. The person in charge of the story is Maya's old school friend Tom, with whom she shares a desk by the window.

Their office, which still smells slightly of bread, overlooks the harbour. On the wall there is a huge map drawn by one of the artists, covered in notes and coffee stains. "That map is the reason the game works," says Maya. "Every place you visit in Lantern Road is a real place in Kelby."

The launch was not easy. The first version had a bug that deleted the saves of players using old laptops, which made a lot of people angry. The team worked for three nights without sleep, during which Tom, according to Maya, ate forty-two sandwiches.

Today, people from all over the world come to Kelby to see the locations from the game, which the town is very happy about. The old baker's sign is still above the door. "Some visitors ask if we still sell bread," Maya says. "Sadly, there's none left. Only games."

texts.title: Who is everyone in this photo?
texts.text:
Liza: OK, you promised to explain this photo. I've looked at it five times and I know nobody except you.
Nick: Right. This was taken at Dan's birthday, which was the night before I left for Portugal. That's why I look so tired.
Liza: Who's the tall guy standing next to the fridge?
Nick: That's Sam, Dan's flatmate. He's the one whose band played at the party. Terrible music, lovely person.
Liza: And the girl talking to him? The one holding the cake?
Nick: That's Vera, who I studied design with. She's now at a studio whose games you play every day, actually. She can't tell me what she's working on, which drives me crazy.
Liza: And those two on the sofa, both of whom look very bored?
Nick: Ha! That's Dan's parents. They came for an hour and stayed until two in the morning. His dad, who is a retired pilot, told me the same story three times.
Liza: What about the man sitting in the corner? He looks like he doesn't know anyone either.
Nick: That's the funny part. Nobody knew him. He came in with a group of people, none of whom had been invited, and ate half of the pizza. Later we found out he lived in the flat below and had come up to complain about the noise.
Liza: And he stayed?
Nick: He stayed, which nobody expected. By midnight he was singing with Sam's band.
Liza: Where was this? It doesn't look like Dan's old flat.
Nick: No, it's the place where he lives now. It's a flat overlooking the river, with a kitchen the size of my whole apartment.
Liza: And what's that thing hanging from the ceiling?
Nick: A piñata made by Vera. It was shaped like Dan's boss. The reason I'm not showing you the next photo is that Dan's boss was also at the party.
Liza: No way!
Nick: Yes. He arrived just as everyone was hitting it with a stick. Fortunately, he has a good sense of humour, without which Dan would be looking for a new job now.
Liza: That is the best party story I've heard all year.
Nick: The last time I saw Dan, he was still apologising.

practice.why: Добавка с запятыми: that нельзя, слово нельзя пропустить → who.

practice.why: Комментарий ко всей фразе → , which.

title: By; noun + предлог; adjective + предлог
summary: Разберёмся со всеми значениями by (by train, by mistake, by Nolan, by 20%, by the window) и выучим «свои» предлоги у существительных и прилагательных: reason for, cause of, increase in, solution to, nice of you, angry with, proud of, keen on, crowded with.

grammar.title: 1. Главная идея: предлог держится за слово, а не за смысл
grammar.html:
Что вы уже знаете: afraid of, good at, interested in, married to (урок A2-17), by accident / on purpose и by Friday (B1-24), written by в пассиве (B1-12), -ing после предлога (B2-3). Теперь собираем полную картину: у многих существительных и прилагательных есть «свой» предлог, и русский перевод тут почти всегда подсказывает неправильно.
Русский

причина чего (без предлога)

решение для проблемы / проблемы

рост цен

злиться на кого-то

похож на

знаменит своими пляжами

English

the reason for the delay

a solution to the problem

a rise in prices

angry with somebody

similar to

famous for its beaches

Учите не слово, а пару: не «reason — причина», а reason for. Так же, как вы учите не «look», а look for / look after. Одна карточка — одно сочетание.

grammar.title: 2. by — «как»: транспорт, оплата, способ, случайность
grammar.html:
by + существительное без артикля отвечает на вопрос «каким способом?». Как только появляется my, the, a — by уходит, и нужен обычный предлог места.
Способ (by, без артикля)Конкретная вещь
by car, by taxiin my car, in a taxi
by train, by bus, by planeon the train, on the 8:15 bus
by bikeon my bike
пешком — on foot(by foot звучит странно)
  • I usually get to the studio by metro, but today I came in Oleg's car. — Обычно я езжу на метро, но сегодня приехал на машине Олега.
  • Is it far? Can we get there on foot? — Туда можно дойти пешком?
  • Can I pay by card? — Можно картой? (by card, by bank transfer; но pay cash или pay in cash)
  • The contract came by post, and I signed it by hand. — Договор пришёл почтой, я подписал его от руки.
  • We'll send you the files by email. — Пришлём файлы по электронной почте.
  • I deleted the wrong layer by mistake. — Я по ошибке удалил не тот слой.
  • We met by chance at a game jam. — Мы случайно познакомились на геймджеме.
I came by my car. · I was by the train. · I'll pay by cash. · We met by a chance.
I came in my car. · I was on the train. · I'll pay in cash. · We met by chance.
Противоположность by mistake / by accident / by chance — on purpose («нарочно»). И запомните: in — в то, во что садятся пригнувшись (car, taxi); on — в то, по чему можно пройти (bus, train, plane, ship).

grammar.title: 3. by — «кем», «чем», «на сколько» и «рядом»
grammar.html:
У by есть ещё три значения: автор / исполнитель, разница в цифрах, рядом с. А инструмент, которым что-то сделали, — не by, а with.
ЗначениеПример
кем сделано (пассив)The level was designed by two interns.
автор произведенияa film by Nolan, a song by Radiohead
на сколько (разница)Sales went up by 20%.
рядом, уMy desk is by the window.

by или with? by — кто (или что) сделал. with — чем, каким инструментом.

  • The icons were drawn by Masha. — Иконки нарисовала Маша. (кто)
  • The icons were drawn with a tablet pen. — Иконки нарисованы стилусом. (чем)
  • The server was hit by a DDoS attack. — На сервер обрушилась DDoS-атака. (причина-«исполнитель» тоже by)
  • Who's this painting by? — Чья это картина? (вопрос об авторе)

Разница в цифрах — очень частое место в новостях и отчётах:

  • We lost by one point. — Мы проиграли с разницей в одно очко.
  • The price has been reduced by half. — Цену снизили вдвое.
  • I missed the bus by two minutes. — Я опоздал на автобус на две минуты.
  • The update cut loading time by three seconds. — Обновление сократило загрузку на три секунды.
The door was opened by a key. · It increased on 20%. · a book of Tolkien
The door was opened with a key. · It increased by 20%. · a book by Tolkien
Русское «на» в «вырос на 20%», «опоздал на 5 минут» → by. Другие by вы уже знаете: by Friday — не позже (B1-24), by myself — сам, один, by doing — тем, что делаешь (B2-3).

grammar.title: 4. Существительное + for / of / in: reason for, cause of, increase in
grammar.html:
Здесь три группы. for — «зачем, для чего нужно»; of — «чего / кого»; in — «рост / падение в чём».
ПредлогСуществительныеПример
forreason, need, demand, excuseThere's no excuse for rudeness.
ofcause, picture, photo, map, plan, drawingWhat was the cause of the crash?
ofadvantage, disadvantageThe main advantage of remote work is time.
inincrease, decrease, rise, fallThere's been a sharp rise in prices.
  • There's a huge demand for pixel artists right now. — На пиксель-художников сейчас огромный спрос.
  • Is there any need for a second meeting? — Есть ли необходимость во второй встрече?
  • She sent me a photo of her new setup. — Она прислала фото своего нового сетапа.
  • We noticed a big fall in the number of new players. — Мы заметили сильное падение числа новых игроков.

Тонкость с advantage: «преимущество чего-то» — of; «есть преимущества в том, чтобы…» — in или to + -ing.

  • The advantage of a big monitor is obvious.
  • There are many advantages in working from home. = There are many advantages to working from home.

reason for, но cause of — это пара, на которой ошибаются даже продвинутые. reason — объяснение, «почему». cause — то, что вызвало событие.

rise in или rise by? in — в чём рост, by — на сколько (см. блок 3): a rise in prices, но prices rose by 10%. Бывает и вместе: a 10% rise in prices.

the reason of the bug · an increase of sales · a demand on the product
the reason for the bug · an increase in sales · a demand for the product

grammar.title: 5. Существительное + to / with / between: solution to, relationship with
grammar.html:
to — «ответ, реакция, доступ к чему-то». with — связь с кем-то одним. between — связь или разница между двумя.
ПредлогСуществительные
tosolution, answer, reply, reaction, key, invitation, damage, attitude (to / towards)
withrelationship, connection, contact
betweendifference, relationship, connection, contact (двух сторон)
  • We still haven't found a solution to the lag problem. — Мы так и не нашли решения проблемы с лагами.
  • I'm still waiting for a reply to my email. — Я всё ещё жду ответа на письмо.
  • The players' reaction to the trailer was amazing. — Реакция игроков на трейлер была потрясающей.
  • Did you get an invitation to the launch party? — Тебе пришло приглашение на вечеринку в честь запуска?
  • The flood caused serious damage to the office. — Потоп нанёс офису серьёзный ущерб.
  • His attitude to feedback has changed a lot. — Его отношение к критике сильно изменилось.
  • I have a great relationship with my art director. — У меня отличные отношения с арт-директором.
  • Do you keep in contact with your old team? — Ты поддерживаешь связь со старой командой?
  • What's the difference between UX and UI? — В чём разница между UX и UI?
a solution of the problem · the answer on my question · an invitation on the party · a relationship to her
a solution to the problem · the answer to my question · an invitation to the party · a relationship with her
Представьте стрелку →: ответ летит к вопросу, ключ подходит к двери, реакция — на новость, урон — по машине. Везде, где есть такая стрелка, — to.

grammar.title: 6. Прилагательное + предлог 1: люди и чувства
grammar.html:
Прилагательные о поведении и эмоциях часто меняют предлог в зависимости от того, на кого или на что направлено чувство.

nice of или nice to?

  • It was really kind of you to review my portfolio. — Очень мило с твоей стороны, что посмотрел моё портфолио. (оценка поступка: of + кто + to do; так же stupid, silly, generous, rude, honest, polite of sb)
  • It was stupid of me to forget my charger. — Глупо было с моей стороны забыть зарядку.
  • The moderators were very rude to him. — Модераторы были с ним очень грубы. (отношение к человеку: nice / kind / rude / friendly / cruel to sb)
СочетаниеПример
pleased / happy / delighted / disappointed with что-то полученноеThe client was delighted with the new logo.
surprised / shocked / amazed at или byI was shocked by the ending.
excited / worried / nervous aboutI'm a bit nervous about the demo.
impressed with или byWe were really impressed with your test task.
fed up / bored withI'm bored with this map.
tired of (надоело)I'm tired of fixing the same bug.

angry, annoyed, furious, upset: about — из-за чего, with — на кого, for — за что.

  • Fans are furious about the new prices. — Фанаты в ярости из-за новых цен.
  • Are you still annoyed with me for missing the stream? — Ты всё ещё злишься на меня за то, что я пропустил стрим?

sorry: about — ситуация; for / about — то, что вы сделали; feel sorry for — жалеть человека.

  • Sorry about the noise — the neighbours are renovating. — Извини за шум.
  • Sorry for interrupting. = Sorry about interrupting. = Sorry I interrupted.
  • I feel sorry for the new guy — he got the worst task. — Мне жаль новичка.
angry on him · nice with me · I feel sorry about Max · tired from waiting (надоело)
angry with him · nice to me · I feel sorry for Max · tired of waiting
tired from тоже бывает, но это «устал физически от»: tired from the trip. А «надоело» — всегда tired of.

grammar.title: 7. Прилагательное + предлог 2: proud of, keen on, crowded with
grammar.html:
Самая большая группа — прилагательные с of. Остальные надо запомнить поштучно. После всех этих предлогов глагол — с -ing: capable of leading a team, keen on streaming.
ofПример
afraid, scared, frightened, terrifiedShe's terrified of public speaking.
fond, proud, ashamed, jealous, enviousI'm really proud of this project.
suspicious, critical, tolerantPlayers are suspicious of free games.
aware, consciousAre you aware of the risks?
capable / incapableShe's capable of leading a team.
typicalIt's typical of him to be late.
full, shortWe're short of time.
ДругиеПример
good / bad / brilliant / hopeless atI'm hopeless at drawing hands.
similar toThis UI is similar to Figma.
different from (или to)It's different from what I expected.
dependent on, но independent ofI don't want to be dependent on one client.
interested inAre you interested in motion design?
famous for, responsible forWho's responsible for the menus?
sure / certain of или aboutAre you sure about that?
keen onI'm not very keen on horror games.
crowded with, но full ofThe hall was crowded with fans.
married / engaged toShe's engaged to a sound designer.

married to кого-то, но married with children — «женат, и есть дети»: He's married with two kids.

similar with · famous by · dependent from · crowded of people · good in maths · jealous on her
similar to · famous for · dependent on · crowded with people · good at maths · jealous of her
Русское «от» почти всегда обманывает: «зависеть от» — depend on, «независимый от» — independent of, «отличаться от» — different from. Три разных предлога на одно «от».

grammar.title: 8. Типичные ошибки — проверьте себя
grammar.html:
I came here by my car.
I came here in my car. / I came here by car.
Sales grew on 30%.
Sales grew by 30%.

texts.title: Patch 1.3: what went wrong
texts.text:
Last month our small studio released patch 1.3 for our strategy game, and for about a week it felt like the end of the world.

The patch was supposed to be a small one. It fixed a few bugs, improved the menus and added a new map. The map was designed by Lena, our youngest level designer, and she was very proud of it. The rest of us were impressed with it too: it was full of hidden paths and looked similar to a real mountain valley.

The first reaction to the patch was positive. Then, on the second day, we noticed a sudden fall in the number of active players. At the same time there was a sharp increase in angry reviews. Players were furious about one thing: their old saves didn't load any more. Some of them had spent hundreds of hours on those saves.

Our producer, Denis, called an emergency meeting. At first, everybody was looking for someone to be angry with. "Who is responsible for the save system?" Denis asked. The answer was me. I felt terrible. I wasn't aware of any problem, because I had tested the patch on a new save, not an old one. It was a typical mistake, and I was ashamed of it.

But Denis wasn't interested in blaming people. "I don't care whose fault it is," he said. "We need a solution to the problem, not a reason for it." So we split into two groups. One group searched for the cause of the bug. The other wrote a message to the players. We apologised, explained what had happened and promised a fix within 48 hours.

The cause turned out to be tiny: one line of code had been deleted by mistake. We fixed it in twenty minutes, but testing took two days. This time we tested it on every kind of save we could find.

When patch 1.3.1 came out, the number of players went up by 40% in a single weekend. Many people wrote that they were surprised by our honesty. One player said: "It was kind of you to explain everything instead of hiding." Our relationship with the community actually became better than before.

What did I learn? The advantage of making a mistake in public is that you can't pretend it didn't happen. And now I'm a little less nervous about releases, because I know what our team is capable of.

texts.title: Road trip to the expo
texts.text:
Kira: So, how are we getting to the game expo? By train or by car?
Artem: I was thinking of going in my car. It's cheaper for four people, and we can stop wherever we want.
Kira: Your car? The one with no air conditioning? I'm not keen on spending six hours in an oven.
Artem: Fair point. Then by train. There's one at 7:10 that arrives just before the doors open.
Kira: Perfect. I've got a photo of the timetable somewhere. Oh, and can we pay by card on the train, or only in cash?
Artem: By card, I think. But let's buy the tickets online. The demand for tickets is huge this year — the whole city will be crowded with gamers.
Kira: True. By the way, it was really nice of you to get us the press passes. How did you do that?
Artem: My cousin is responsible for the indie section. She's very fond of our game, so she sent me an invitation.
Kira: That's so kind of her! I'm a bit nervous about our demo, though. What if the build crashes in front of everyone?
Artem: It won't. And if it does, we'll say it was on purpose — "a surprise boss fight".
Kira: Very funny. Seriously, I'm tired of hearing that our game is similar to that other farming game. It's completely different from it!
Artem: Don't worry. Anyone who plays for five minutes will see the difference between them. Ours has dragons.
Kira: Good answer. What about Pasha? Is he coming? He was annoyed with us for not inviting him last year.
Artem: He's coming. He was upset about it for a month, but now he's excited about the trip. He's even learned the whole route by heart.
Kira: Typical of Pasha. And the hotel? Is it far from the station?
Artem: Ten minutes on foot. It's by the river, and apparently the rooms are small but clean. I'm not sure about the breakfast, though.
Kira: As long as there's coffee, I'll survive. I'm sorry about all the questions, by the way. I just want everything to go well.
Artem: Don't be sorry. It's typical of good producers to ask questions. And I'm sure people will be impressed with the demo.
Kira: I hope you're right. See you at the station at 6:45!

title: Глагол + предлог: at, about, for, of, from, on, into, with
summary: Выучим, какой предлог нужен после десятков частых глаголов (explain to, shout at, apply for, think of / about, hear from, accuse of, blame on, rely on, believe in, succeed in, spend on), где предлог не нужен вовсе (call you, discuss it, answer the email) и как один предлог меняет смысл глагола.

grammar.title: 1. Главная идея: глагол и предлог — одна единица
grammar.html:
Что вы уже знаете (урок A2-17): listen to, wait for, depend on, look at / for / after и то, что call, text, discuss работают без предлога. В уроке B2-3 — insist on doing, succeed in doing. Теперь проходим глаголы с предлогами систематично, по предлогам, и смотрим, как смена предлога меняет смысл: shout at и shout to, think of и think about, hear of и hear from.
Русский

объясни мне

ответь на письмо

поздравить с релизом

состоять из

обвинить в

тратить на

English

explain it to me

answer _ the email

congratulate on the release

consist of

accuse of

spend on

Три типа ловушек: 1) предлог другой, чем в русском (поздравить с → congratulate on); 2) в русском предлог есть, а в английском нет (ответить на → answer); 3) в русском нет, а в английском есть (объяснить мне → explain to me).

grammar.title: 2. to — или вообще без предлога: explain to, но call, answer, ask
grammar.html:
После explain, describe, apologise, talk, listen, write, reply человеку нужен to. А call, phone, text, email, answer, ask, discuss берут человека или предмет напрямую.
С toБез предлога
explain the task to the teamcall the client, text me
describe to me what happenedanswer the email
apologise to her for the delayask the manager
talk / speak to him (можно with)discuss the plan
reply to the emailthank him for the help
write to the publisheremail the publisher

explain / describe + вопросительное слово: человек идёт с to и стоит до what / why / how.

  • I explained to them why the release was late. — Я объяснил им, почему релиз задержался.
  • Can you describe to me what the error looks like? — Опиши мне, как выглядит ошибка.
  • He apologised to the players for the bug. — Он извинился перед игроками за баг.
  • She never answers my messages, but she always replies to Max. — answer без предлога, reply to.
Explain me this rule. · He apologised me. · Answer to my question. · I called to the bank.
Explain this rule to me. · He apologised to me. · Answer my question. · I called the bank.
answer и reply означают одно и то же, но reply всегда хочет to. Можно запомнить так: «ре-плай ту» звучит как одно слово.

grammar.title: 3. at или to: shout at — «на», shout to — «чтобы услышал»
grammar.html:
at — направлено в цель, часто с агрессией или вниманием. to — передаём человеку, чтобы он услышал или поймал.
at (в цель)Пример
look, stare, glance at; have / take a look atTake a look at this mockup.
laugh atEveryone laughed at my avatar.
aim, point, shoot, fire atAim at the head and shoot at the red barrels.

Две пары, где предлог полностью меняет смысл:

  • The coach shouted at us after we lost. — Тренер наорал на нас. (злость → at)
  • She shouted to me from the other side of the hall. — Она крикнула мне с другого конца зала. (чтобы я услышал → to)
  • Somebody threw a bottle at the stage. — Кто-то швырнул бутылку в сцену. (попасть → at)
  • Throw the ball to me! — Кинь мне мяч! (чтобы поймал → to)
Don't laugh on me. · Look on this! · He stared to me.
Don't laugh at me. · Look at this! · He stared at me.
Русское «смеяться над», «смотреть на», «целиться в» — в английском всё это одно at. Где цель — там at.

grammar.title: 4. about, for, after: apply for, search for, look after, care about
grammar.html:
about — тема («о чём»). for — цель, то, что хотим получить. У care и look смысл полностью зависит от предлога.
ГлаголПример
talk / read / know aboutWhat do you know about Unreal Engine?
do something / nothing aboutWe have to do something about the lag.
apply (to a company) for a jobI applied to three studios for a junior role.
ask (sb) for — попросить что-тоI asked them for more time.
search (a place) forI searched the whole flat for my headphones.
leave (a place) for — уехать вShe left Moscow for Berlin.
wait for sth to happenI'm waiting for the build to finish.

Три тонкости:

  • We had a long discussion about the budget. — но We discussed the budget. (существительное discussion — с about, глагол discuss — без)
  • Can I ask you the time? · I asked a local the way. — спросить время, дорогу — без for
  • She left for work at eight. — Она ушла на работу. (не left to work)
СочетаниеСмыслПример
care aboutсчитать важнымHe only cares about money.
care for / look after / take care ofзаботиться, ухаживатьWho looks after your cat?
not care forне любитьI don't care for spicy food.
care + what / how / ifбез aboutI don't care what they think.
look forискатьI'm looking for a new job.

take care of — ещё и «взять на себя»: Don't worry, I'll take care of the tickets.

Let's discuss about it. · I'm applying on this job. · She left to Kazan. · I don't care about what they say.
Let's discuss it. · I'm applying for this job. · She left for Kazan. · I don't care what they say.

grammar.title: 5. about или of: hear, think, dream, complain, remind
grammar.html:
Эти пять глаголов — самые коварные: предлог меняет смысл, и русский перевод не помогает.
СочетаниеСмыслПример
hear aboutузнать новостьDid you hear about the layoffs?
hear ofзнать, что существуетI've never heard of this studio.
hear fromполучить весточкуHave you heard from Lena lately?
think aboutобдумыватьI'll think about your offer.
think ofпридумать; мнениеWho thought of this name? · What do you think of it?
dream aboutвидеть во снеI dreamt about the deadline again.
dream of / about + -ingмечтатьI dream of making my own game.
complain (to sb) aboutжаловаться наWe complained to the landlord about the noise.
complain ofжаловаться на больHe complained of a headache.
remind sb aboutнапомнить, чтобы не забылRemind me about the call.
remind sb ofнапоминать, быть похожимThis game reminds me of my childhood.
  • We're thinking of moving to Tbilisi. = We're thinking about moving to Tbilisi. — Подумываем переехать. (про возможные планы — оба)
  • I couldn't think of anything to say. — Мне ничего не пришло в голову. (придумать → только of)
  • I didn't think much of the finale. — Финал мне не особо понравился.
  • Cheat? I wouldn't dream of it! — Жульничать? Да ни за что!
I've never heard from this game. · I'll think of it and tell you tomorrow. · She reminds me about my sister.
I've never heard of this game. · I'll think about it and tell you tomorrow. · She reminds me of my sister.
from — «от кого пришло» (письмо, звонок). of у remind — «похож на», у hear — «слышал о существовании». about — «на тему».

grammar.title: 6. of, for, from, on: accuse of, blame for, suffer from, rely on
grammar.html:
Глаголы обвинения, благодарности, защиты и зависимости. Структура часто такая: глагол + кого + предлог + что. После предлога — существительное или -ing.
ПредлогГлаголыПример
ofaccuse / suspect sb ofThey accused him of cheating.
ofapprove / disapprove of; consist ofThe team consists of six people.
of / fromdie of / fromMy laptop died from overheating.
forthank / forgive / blame sb for; apologise for; pay forI'll never forgive them for cancelling the show.
fromsuffer from; protect sb / sth fromThis case protects the phone from falls.
ondepend / rely on; live on; congratulate / compliment sb onCongratulations on the release!

blame — два порядка слов:

  • They blamed me for the crash. — Меня обвинили в вылете. (blame кого for что)
  • They blamed the crash on me. — Вину за вылет свалили на меня. (blame что on кого)
  • Who is to blame for this mess? — Кто виноват в этом бардаке?

pay for, но pay the bill: платим за вещь, но сам счёт, аренду, налог, штраф — без предлога.

  • Who paid for the pizza? — Кто заплатил за пиццу?
  • I need to pay the rent and the internet bill. — Мне нужно заплатить за аренду и интернет.
  • You can rely on Nika — she never misses a deadline. — На Нику можно положиться.
  • Freelancers can't always live on one project. — Фрилансеру не всегда хватает на жизнь одного проекта.
  • Will you buy it? — It depends how much it costs. (перед how / what / when можно без on)
She accused me in lying. · Congratulations with your birthday! · The course consists from ten lessons. · I paid the coffee.
She accused me of lying. · Congratulations on your birthday! (или просто Happy birthday!) · The course consists of ten lessons. · I paid for the coffee.
Самая частая ошибка русскоговорящих — «поздравляю с» → congratulations with. Правильно только on: поздравление «ложится на» событие.

grammar.title: 7. in, into, with, to, on: believe in, crash into, provide with, spend on
grammar.html:
Последняя большая группа. into — удар или деление на части; with — «наполнить, снабдить чем»; on — «сосредоточить, потратить на».
ПредлогГлаголыПример
inbelieve in, specialise in, succeed inOur studio specialises in pixel art.
intobreak into; crash / drive / bump / run intoSomeone broke into my account.
intodivide / split / cut into; translate from … intoLet's split the task into three parts.
withcollide with; fill with; provide / supply sb withThe studio provides us with laptops.
tohappen to; invite to; prefer X to YI prefer dark mode to light mode.
onconcentrate on, insist on, spend onHow much do you spend on games?

believe или believe in?

  • I don't believe him. — Я ему не верю. (считаю, что он врёт)
  • I don't believe the rumours. — Я не верю слухам. (что это правда)
  • Do you believe in ghosts? — Ты веришь в привидения? (что существуют)
  • I believe in giving honest feedback. — Я считаю, что правильно давать честный фидбек. (что это хорошо)
  • I finally succeeded in fixing the build. — Мне наконец удалось починить сборку.
  • I bumped into my old teacher at the mall. — Я случайно встретил бывшего учителя. (bump / run into — ещё и «случайно встретить»)
  • The game has been translated into twelve languages. — Игру перевели на двенадцать языков.
  • Fill the bottle with water. — Налей в бутылку воды. (fill with, но full of — B2-9)
  • What happened to your old Twitch channel? — Что стало с твоим старым каналом?
I prefer tea than coffee. · He spent all his money for skins. · Translate it on English. · Concentrate at your work.
I prefer tea to coffee. · He spent all his money on skins. · Translate it into English. · Concentrate on your work.
«Переводить на язык» — into: текст как будто «переливается» в другой язык. А «говорить на языке» — in English (B1-24).

grammar.title: 8. Типичные ошибки — проверьте себя
grammar.html:
Can you explain me the task?
Can you explain the task to me?
Please answer to my email.
Please answer my email. / Please reply to my email.
Don't laugh on him.

We discussed about the new level.

I've never heard from this band.

Итог юнита в одной строке

texts.title: Somebody broke into my account
texts.text:
Last Tuesday I woke up to forty-seven notifications. At first I thought people were congratulating me on something. Then I read them. Someone had broken into my gaming account overnight and spent all my savings on skins.

I've always believed in strong passwords, so I couldn't understand how it had happened. I searched my inbox for any suspicious emails and finally found one: a fake "security check" that I had clicked on a week before. I was furious — not with the hackers, but with myself.

The first thing I did was contact support. I described to them exactly what had happened and explained that I hadn't made any of those purchases. The reply came quickly, but it was a template: "We are sorry to hear about your problem. Please wait for a specialist to contact you." So I waited. And waited.

Meanwhile, my friend Gleb called me. He had heard about the hack from our clan chat. "Did you use the same password for your email?" he asked. I didn't want to answer him, because the honest answer was yes. He didn't laugh at me, though. He just said, "Change it now. Then we'll think about the rest."

He was right. I changed every password, turned on two-factor authentication and asked my bank to block the card. The bank was great: they didn't accuse me of lying, they simply refunded the money within three days.

The game company was a different story. Four days later a specialist finally wrote to me. At first he seemed to blame the problem on me: "Our system cannot protect users from their own mistakes." I complained to his manager about his tone, and after that things moved faster. They didn't give me the skins back, but they restored my progress and apologised for the delay.

A week later, my account was mine again. I was relieved, but I also learned a few things. You can't rely on support to fix everything. You shouldn't use one password for everything. And you should never click on a link just because it looks official.

Now, whenever I get an email that asks me to "confirm my details", it reminds me of that Tuesday morning. I don't click. I delete it — and I think of Gleb, who still hasn't let me forget it.

texts.title: The job offer
texts.text:
Dasha: Hey! Did you hear from the studio in Belgrade?
Ilya: Yes, this morning. They offered me the job!
Dasha: No way! Congratulations on the offer! So when do you leave for Belgrade?
Ilya: Hold on, I haven't said yes yet. I'm still thinking about it.
Dasha: What is there to think about? You've been dreaming of working on a big game for years.
Ilya: I know. But it's complicated. The team consists of forty people, and I'd be responsible for the whole interface. At my current job we're five, and I can concentrate on the things I love.
Dasha: That sounds like fear talking. You're capable of much more than menus for a match-three game.
Ilya: Maybe. But I care about my current team. I don't want them to think I've left them in the middle of a project.
Dasha: Have you talked to your boss about it?
Ilya: Not yet. I'm afraid he'll blame me for delaying our release.
Dasha: He won't. He's the one who always insists on "growing as a designer". And anyway, you can't depend on one small studio forever.
Ilya: True. Oh, and there's another thing. They asked me for a test task last week, and I think I did it in a rush. When they described to me what they wanted, I only understood half of it.
Dasha: And they still offered you the job. That tells you what they think of you.
Ilya: Fair. The art director even complimented me on the colour choices.
Dasha: See? What about money? Is it enough to live on over there?
Ilya: More than enough. They'll pay for the flat for the first three months and provide me with all the equipment.
Dasha: Then I really don't understand the problem.
Ilya: The problem is that everything reminds me of the first time I moved. I was lonely for a year.
Dasha: That was different. You didn't know anybody. Now you've got me, and I'll call you every weekend. I'll even learn some Serbian so you can explain the jokes to me.
Ilya: Ha. OK. I'll talk to my boss tomorrow and reply to them by Friday.
Dasha: Promise?
Ilya: Promise. And remind me about it on Thursday, in case I lose my nerve.

title: Фразовые глаголы 1: in, out, on, off
summary: Разберёмся, как частицы in, out, on, off меняют смысл глагола, где ставить объект в длинных и трёхсловных фразовых глаголах, как они ведут себя в пассиве — и выучим десятки живых глаголов из игр, сериалов и чатов: work out, turn out, find out, call off, put off, get on with, show off, rip off.

grammar.title: 1. Главная идея: частица — это английская приставка
grammar.html:
Что вы уже знаете (урок A2-17): фразовый глагол — это глагол + частица (give up, log in, turn it off, run out of), и местоимение встаёт в середину. На B2 идём глубже: у частицы есть свой смысл, один глагол часто имеет несколько значений, бывают глаголы из трёх слов, они живут в пассиве и превращаются в существительные.
Русский

Выяснить, кто это был.

Вычислить сумму.

Отменить матч.

Отложить релиз.

Задремать на лекции.

Продолжать играть.

English

Find out who it was.

Work out the total.

Call off the match.

Put off the release.

Doze off in a lecture.

Carry on playing.

Русская приставка меняет глагол так же, как английская частица: ходить → выходить = go → go out. Удобно держать в голове пары: вы- ≈ out (выйти, выяснить, выбросить, вычеркнуть), от- ≈ off (отменить, отложить, отъехать, отключиться), про- / дальше ≈ on (продолжать, проехать дальше).

Частица бывает двух видов:

Что делает частицаПримерПеревод
направление — смысл угадываетсяThe bus was full, so we couldn't get on.…не смогли сесть
направлениеHe jumped in the car and drove off.…и уехал
новый смысл — надо учитьHow did you get on at the interview?Как прошло собеседование?
новый смыслMy English is good enough to get by.…чтобы как-то справляться
Главный список частиц: in, out, on, off, up, down, away, back + реже by, through, about, along, over, forward, round. В этом уроке — первые четыре, в следующем — остальные.

grammar.title: 2. Грамматика: где объект, три слова, пассив
grammar.html:
Правило «it — в середину» вы знаете. Теперь — всё остальное: длинный объект, глаголы из трёх слов и пассив.
ТипКакПример
без объектапросто глагол + частицаThe plane took off.
объект — словодо или после частицыTurn on the light. = Turn the light on.
объект — it / them / meтолько в серединуTurn it on.
объект длинныйлучше после частицыTurn off all the lights in the kitchen.
три словаобъект — в самом концеI can't get out of it.

Три слова: фразовый глагол + предлог. Разрывать нельзя, местоимение — в конец:

  • I'm looking forward to the new season. — Жду не дождусь нового сезона.
  • Slow down! I can't keep up with you. — Я за тобой не успеваю.
  • Why did you run away from me? — Почему ты от меня убежал?
  • I promised to help. I can't get out of it now. — Теперь не отверчусь.
  • We've run out of potions. — У нас кончились зелья.
  • She dropped out of university after a year. — Она бросила университет через год.
После look forward to — существительное или -ing (урок b2-3): I'm looking forward to seeing you. Здесь to — предлог, а не часть инфинитива.

Пассив: частица остаётся на месте, сразу после причастия.

  • The final was called off because of the storm. — Финал отменили.
  • The experiment was carried out in 2024. — Эксперимент провели в 2024.
  • He said he was a bank manager, and I was completely taken in. — Я полностью повёлся.
  • Fifty euros for a cable? You got ripped off. — Тебя развели.
The match was called because of the rain. · I can't get out it. · I'm looking forward to see you.
The match was called off. · I can't get out of it. · I'm looking forward to seeing you.

grammar.title: 3. IN и OUT: внутрь, наружу — и не только
grammar.html:
in — внутрь (в комнату, машину, систему), out — наружу. Без объекта говорим in / out, с местом — into / out of.
inoutСмысл
get inget outсесть в / выйти из (машины)
move inmove outвъехать / съехать (с квартиры)
check incheck outзаселиться, зарегистрироваться / выписаться
let somebody inlet somebody outвпустить / выпустить
break in—вломиться
—be locked outне попасть домой (ключи внутри)
  • I'm moving in on Friday. = I'm moving into my new flat on Friday.
  • She climbed out. = She climbed out of the pool.
  • I left my keys inside and got locked out. — Ключи остались внутри, я не мог попасть домой.

Другие глаголы с in — смысл уже не просто «внутрь»:

ГлаголЗначениеПример
fill in / fill outзаполнить (форму)Fill in the form and send it to HR.
drop in (on sb)заскочить без договорённостиDrop in if you're in the area.
join inподключиться к тому, что уже идётThey were playing cards, so I joined in.
take sb inобмануть, провестиDon't be taken in by fake giveaways.
plug inвключить в розеткуIs the router plugged in?
hand inсдать (работу)Hand in your designs by Friday.
give inуступить, сдатьсяHe kept asking, and in the end I gave in.

Другие глаголы с out:

ГлаголЗначениеПример
eat outпоесть в кафе, не домаLet's eat out tonight.
drop out (of)бросить (учёбу, гонку), выбытьTwo teams dropped out of the tournament.
get out of sthотвертеться от обещанногоHow did you get out of the meeting?
leave outпропустить, не включитьYou left out my name. I feel left out.
cross outвычеркнутьCross out the names of people who can't come.
I moved in my new flat. · I'll drop in you tomorrow.
I moved into my new flat. · I'll drop in on you tomorrow. / I'll drop in to see you.
feel left out — «чувствовать себя лишним, будто тебя не позвали»: Everyone had a team except me. I felt left out.

grammar.title: 4. OUT глубже: work out, turn out, find out, sort out
grammar.html:
out часто значит «до результата»: выяснить, вычислить, разобраться, довести до конца. А ещё — «погаснуть, исчезнуть».

out = погасить, погаснуть: All the lights went out. — Погас весь свет. · Put out the fire! — Потуши огонь! · Turn the lights out. · Blow out the candles. — Задуй свечи.

work out — один глагол, пять значений:

ЗначениеПример
тренироватьсяI work out three times a week. (a workout — тренировка)
сложиться (хорошо)I hope everything works out for you.
не сложилосьWe tried working together, but it didn't work out.
получается (по деньгам)Ninety euros for three — that works out at thirty each.
вычислить; разобратьсяI can't work out why the build crashes. = I can't figure out why…

Другие важные глаголы с out:

ГлаголЗначениеПример
find out (that / what / about)узнать, выяснитьI just found out that the game is free this week.
turn out (to be / that)оказаться (в итоге)The new guy turned out to be really funny.
carry outпровести, выполнить (план, опрос)We carried out a survey of 500 players.
point out (to sb)указать, обратить вниманиеThanks for pointing out the typo.
sort outуладить; разобратьDon't worry, I'll sort it out.
give out / hand outраздать каждомуThey handed out free keys at the expo.
run out (of)кончитьсяWe ran out of time. · Time ran out.
try outопробоватьWe're trying out a new design tool.

turn out — три конструкции:

  • He turned out to be right. — Он оказался прав.
  • It turned out that they had never met. — Оказалось, что они никогда не встречались.
  • The morning was grey, but the day turned out nice. — День в итоге выдался хорошим.
I knew about it only yesterday. — «узнал вчера» · It was turned out that he lied.
I found out about it only yesterday. · It turned out that he had lied.
Русское «узнать» — два английских глагола: know — знать (состояние), find out — узнать (момент, когда информация пришла). «Я узнал вчера» — всегда found out.

grammar.title: 5. ON и OFF (1): техника, события, одежда, «прочь»
grammar.html:
on / off — включено / выключено, идёт / отменено, на себе / снято. А off ещё значит «прочь, в путь».

Техника: Is the heating on? — Отопление включено? · Leave the lights on. — Оставь свет включённым. · Let's put some music on. · I'll put the kettle on. — Поставлю чайник.

События:

ГлаголЗначениеПример
go onпроисходитьWhat's going on here?
be onидти (в кино, по ТВ), состоятьсяIs the match still on?
call offотменитьThey called off the concert.
put off (+ -ing)отложитьStop putting off calling the client.

Одежда и тело: put on (надеть; put on weight — набрать вес), try on (примерить), take off (снять).

  • I've put on three kilos since the release. — Я набрал три кило после релиза.
  • Take off your shoes, please. — Разуйтесь, пожалуйста.

off = прочь, в путь:

ГлаголЗначениеПример
set offотправиться в путьWe set off at dawn.
take offвзлететь; резко стать популярнымThe game took off on TikTok.
see sb offпроводить (на вокзал)We went to the airport to see her off.
be off (to)уходить, уезжатьI'm off to Berlin tomorrow. · I'm off. — Я пошёл.
drive / run / ride offуехать / убежать / укатитьShe jumped on her bike and rode off.
What is going? · I'm wearing my coat — выхожу через минуту. · We put off to decide.
What's going on? · I'm putting on my coat. · We put off deciding.
put on — действие (надеть), wear — состояние (быть одетым). «Она надевает куртку» — putting on; «Она в куртке» — wearing.

grammar.title: 6. ON и OFF (2): продолжать, ладить, задремать, развести
grammar.html:
on часто значит «дальше, продолжать». У off — пучок значений: задремать, сработать, выпендриваться, отругать, доделать, развести на деньги, отбить охоту.

on = продолжать (go on / carry on / keep on doing вы видели в B1):

  • The party went on until four. — Вечеринка продолжалась до четырёх.
  • Please carry on with what you're doing. — Продолжайте, я не мешаю.
  • He keeps on sending me memes at 3 a.m. — Он всё время шлёт мне мемы в три ночи. (раздражает)
  • Don't stop here — let's drive on to the next town. — Поехали дальше.

get on — три смысла:

КонструкцияЗначениеПример
get onкак успехиHow are you getting on in your new job?
get on (well) with sbладитьI get on really well with my team.
get on with sthзаняться делом, продолжитьRight, I must get on with my work.

off — учим по одному:

ГлаголЗначениеПример
doze / drop / nod offзадрематьI dozed off during the lecture.
go offсработать (будильник); испортиться (еда)My alarm didn't go off. · The milk has gone off.
show offвыпендриваться, хвастатьсяHe's just showing off his new skin.
tell sb offотругатьMy boss told me off for missing the deadline.
finish offдоделать; добитьI'll finish it off tomorrow. · Finish him off!
rip sb offобдирать, развести на деньгиForty euros for that? You were ripped off.
put sb off (sth / doing)отбить охотуThe long queue put us off.
put off — два разных смысла: «отложить» (We put off the meeting.) и «отбить желание» (What put you off applying? — Что тебя отпугнуло от заявки?). Если объект — человек, почти всегда второе.
I get on with my brother good. · He keeps on to call me. · Carry on to work.
I get on well with my brother. · He keeps (on) calling me. · Carry on working. / Carry on with your work.

grammar.title: 7. Большая таблица: in, out, on, off в играх, сериалах и чатах
grammar.html:
Эти глаголы вы будете слышать каждый день — в войс-чате, в комментариях, в сериалах. Смысл многих уже угадывается по частице.

Игры и стримы

EnglishЗначениеПример
log on / log offзайти / выйти из сетиI'll log on after dinner.
hop on / jump inбыстро зайти (в игру, созвон)Hop on Discord, we're starting.
take outубрать, уничтожить (врага)Take out the sniper first.
wipe outуничтожить всехOur whole squad got wiped out.
knock outвырубить, выбить из турнираWe got knocked out in the semi-final.
hold off / fight offсдерживать / отбитьсяHold them off for ten seconds!
pull offпровернуть (сложное)I can't believe we pulled that off!
back offотступить, отстатьBack off, they have a tank!
kick offначаться (матч, турнир)The finals kick off at eight.
cash outвывести деньги / забрать выигрышI cashed out before the crash.

Сериалы и кино

EnglishЗначениеПример
come outвыйти (о фильме, игре)The new season comes out in May.
drag onзатягиватьсяThe middle of the season really drags on.
kill offубить персонажа (о сценаристах)They killed off my favourite character!
write outвывести из сериалаThe actor left, so they wrote him out.
catch onстать популярнымThe show didn't catch on in Europe.
tune inвключить, смотреть трансляциюTune in on Friday for the finale.
zone outотключиться, «выпасть»Sorry, I zoned out. Who's that guy?
sell outраспродать; продаться (о человеке)The tickets sold out in an hour.

Чаты и разговор

EnglishЗначениеПример
check outзацени, посмотриCheck out this clip!
hang outтусоватьсяWanna hang out this weekend?
chill outрасслабься, успокойсяChill out, it's just a game.
freak outзапаниковать, психанутьDon't freak out, but I deleted the file.
count me in / outя в деле / я пасPizza and a movie? Count me in!
back out (of)отказаться от обещанногоTwo players backed out at the last minute.
reach out (to)связаться, написатьFeel free to reach out if you have questions.
call outпублично указать на ошибкуHe got called out for cheating.
stand outвыделятьсяYour portfolio really stands out.

Существительные из фразовых глаголов — пишутся слитно или через дефис, ударение на первую часть:

ГлаголСуществительноеПример
work outa workout — тренировкаa quick morning workout
rip offa rip-off — развод, обдираловкаThis DLC is a total rip-off.
show offa show-off — хвастунDon't be such a show-off.
spin offa spin-off — спин-оффa spin-off about the villain

texts.title: Launch night
texts.text:
Last Friday our studio launched its first online game, Night Harbour. I'm the UI designer on the team, and I want to describe what happened while I still remember every detail.

We had planned everything carefully. The servers were ready, the trailer was out, and more than twenty thousand people had signed up for launch night. At seven o'clock the whole team gathered at the office. Somebody put some music on, somebody else put the kettle on, and our producer, Vera, handed out pizza and energy drinks. The launch was at nine.

At half past eight the lights in the office suddenly went out. For a moment nobody said anything. Then our lead programmer, Kostya, started to freak out. It turned out that a cleaner had plugged in a huge heater in the corridor and the whole floor had lost power. Our servers were in a data centre, so the game itself was fine, but we couldn't log on to anything. Someone pointed out that we could still work from our phones, so we carried on like that for twenty minutes until the power came back on.

At nine the game went live. Within ten minutes, thirty thousand players had logged on — far more than we had expected. The login queue got longer and longer, and players started to complain in the chat. Some of them logged off and left angry reviews; one even called the game a total rip-off, although it's free. Kostya and I spent the next hour trying to work out what was going on. In the end we found out that one small setting was wrong. We sorted it out at about eleven, and the queue disappeared.

The funniest moment came at midnight. A famous streamer, who had promised to try the game out live, dozed off in the middle of his stream. His chat went crazy, and when he finally opened his eyes, he just went on playing as if nothing had happened. The clip got two million views, and suddenly everyone wanted to check our game out.

We didn't set off home until three in the morning. Nothing had been called off, nothing had been put off, and the game was working. Looking at the numbers on Saturday, I realised that the night had turned out much better than we had feared. Now I just have to get on with fixing the menus — the players have already pointed out six problems.

texts.title: Is the raid still on?
texts.text:
Max: Hey, is the raid still on for tonight? Lena said something about calling it off.
Lena: It's not called off, just put off. Den can't log on until ten.
Den: Sorry, guys. My boss told me off this morning, so I have to finish off a report first.
Max: Ouch. What happened?
Den: Long story. I left out half the data in a presentation, and nobody pointed it out until the client meeting. It turned out really badly.
Lena: That's awful. But don't freak out — everybody messes up sometimes.
Den: Thanks. Anyway, count me in for ten. Do we have enough potions? Last week we ran out of them in the middle of the boss fight.
Max: I bought fifty yesterday. And I tried out the new healer build. It works out really well — much better than the old one.
Lena: Great. Hey, do you remember that guy from the guild who kept on showing off his gold armour?
Max: Tarkan? What about him?
Lena: He's dropped out. He said our guild was too slow for him, and he's joined some pro team.
Den: Good. He never got on with anybody anyway. He just kept on telling people off in voice chat.
Max: True. Oh, and Lena, did you find out why the game kept crashing on your laptop?
Lena: Yes, I worked it out myself. The laptop wasn't plugged in, so it was running on battery, and the graphics card kept switching off.
Max: Ha! Classic. What about the new expansion? Has it come out yet?
Lena: It comes out next Thursday. I've already checked out the trailer. It looks amazing, but it costs forty euros, which is a bit of a rip-off.
Den: Forty? That puts me off a bit. I'll wait for a sale.
Max: Me too. I got ripped off last year with the deluxe edition, and I'm not doing that again.
Lena: OK, so ten o'clock. Den, don't doze off before then!
Den: No promises. If I'm not on at ten, go on without me and I'll join in later.
Max: Fine, but don't try to get out of it like last time. You said your internet had gone off, and then we saw you online in another game.
Den: That was one time!
Lena: Right, everyone, stop chatting. Den, get on with your report.
Den: Yes, boss. Logging off.

title: Фразовые глаголы 2: up, down, away, back + итог B2
summary: Разберём частицы up, down, away, back — «до конца», «меньше и сломалось», «прочь» и «обратно, в ответ», выучим глаголы с несколькими значениями (bring up, make up, turn down, hold up), большие таблицы для игр, сериалов и чатов — и соберём весь уровень B2 в одну шпаргалку.

grammar.title: 1. Главная идея: у каждой частицы — своя картинка
grammar.html:
Что вы уже знаете (уроки A2-17 и b2-11): pick up, put down, give up, grow up, give back, throw away — и правило it в середину. Теперь запомним картинку каждой частицы — по ней можно угадать смысл незнакомого глагола.
ЧастицаКартинкаПримеры
upвверх; до конца, полностью; появитьсяstand up, use up, tidy up, turn up
downвниз; меньше, тише; сломалось; на бумагуsit down, slow down, break down, write down
awayпрочь, исчезнуть; отдать, убратьrun away, give away, throw away
backобратно; в ответcome back, pay back, call back, smile back
Русский

Доешь, я хочу помыть тарелку.

Сбавь скорость!

Мне отказали.

Он сбежал.

Я тебе перезвоню.

English

Eat up, I want to wash the plate.

Slow down!

I was turned down.

He ran away.

I'll call you back.

up — как русские «до-» и «за-» в смысле «доделать до конца»: доесть = eat up, допить = drink up, заполнить бак = fill up, запереть = lock up. down — «с-»: сбавить, снизить, сломаться, снести.

grammar.title: 2. UP и DOWN: вверх-вниз, меньше, сломалось
grammar.html:
Сначала пары «вверх — вниз», потом down в трёх переносных смыслах: разрушить, уменьшить, остановиться.
updownСмысл
put up (a poster)take downповесить / снять со стены
pick upput downподнять / положить
stand upsit / lie / bend downвстать / сесть, лечь, нагнуться
turn upturn downсделать громче (теплее) / тише

down = разрушить: They knocked down the old cinema. — Старый кинотеатр снесли. · The house burnt down. — Дом сгорел дотла. · Who cut down the tree? · He was knocked down by a car. — Его сбила машина.

down = меньше, спокойнее:

ГлаголЗначениеПример
slow downсбавить скоростьSlow down, you'll crash!
calm (sb) downуспокоиться / успокоитьCalm down, it's just a game.
cut down (on)сократить, меньше употреблятьI'm cutting down on energy drinks.

down = перестало работать:

ГлаголЗначениеПример
break downсломаться (машина); развалиться (отношения, переговоры)Their marriage broke down after a year.
close / shut downзакрыться (бизнес); выключить (систему)The studio shut down last year.

Ещё три важных:

ГлаголЗначениеПример
turn sb / sth downотказать, отклонитьThey offered her the job, but she turned it down.
let sb downподвести, разочароватьI trusted you, and you let me down.
write downзаписатьWrite down the password somewhere safe.

I was refused on the job. · The car was broken down on the way.
I was turned down for the job. · The car broke down on the way. (break down — без объекта, не пассив)

grammar.title: 3. UP (1): вырасти, начать, появиться, догнать
grammar.html:
up — самая «богатая» частица. Здесь — глаголы про жизнь и события: вырасти, основать, увлечься, появиться, оказаться в итоге.
ГлаголЗначениеПример
go / come / walk up (to)подойтиA fan came up to me and asked for a selfie.

bring up a childвырастить, воспитатьShe was brought up by her grandparents.
set upосновать, создать, настроитьTwo friends set up the studio in 2019.
take upзаняться (хобби); занимать (место, время)I took up climbing last year. · The game takes up 90 GB.
turn up / show upприйти, появитьсяWe waited, but he never turned up.
tidy / clean / clear upприбратьсяWho's going to tidy up after the party?
wash upпомыть посудуI'll cook if you wash up.
use upизрасходовать всёI've used up all my free trials.
fix up a meetingдоговориться о встречеLet's fix up a call for Monday.
catch up (with)догнатьGo on, I'll catch up with you.
keep up (with)не отставать; продолжать так жеGreat work! Keep it up!
end up (+ место / -ing)в итоге оказаться, в итоге сделатьWe ended up sleeping at the airport.
make up / be made up ofсоставлять / состоять изWomen make up half of our team.
give up (-ing)бросить, сдатьсяI gave up trying to explain.
  • Our team is made up of three designers and two developers. — Наша команда состоит из трёх дизайнеров и двух разработчиков.
  • I wanted to stay in, but I ended up going to the party. — Хотел остаться дома, а в итоге пошёл на вечеринку.
  • You're too fast — I can't keep up with you. — Я за тобой не успеваю.
My grandmother grew me up. · We ended up to sleep in the car. · I took up to run.
My grandmother brought me up. · We ended up sleeping in the car. · I took up running.
grow up — вырос сам (без объекта), bring up — вырастили тебя (есть объект). Если после end up, give up, take up идёт глагол — только в форме -ing.

grammar.title: 4. UP (2): придумать, помириться, терпеть, задержать
grammar.html:
Здесь глаголы, у которых несколько значений. Особенно коварны make up и bring up — смысл решает контекст.

Один глагол — много смыслов:

ГлаголЗначениеПример

Остальные глаголы с up:

ГлаголЗначениеПример

I can't put up with this noise. · She broke up with her boyfriend. · He made up an excuse.
put up with — три слова, «терпеть через силу». Синоним одним словом — stand / tolerate: I can't stand it.

grammar.html:
away — от дома, от человека, прочь. back — домой, обратно или в ответ на действие.
awayback

grammar.title: 8. Итог B2 — шпаргалка по уровню
grammar.html:
Поздравляем: вы прошли весь уровень B2 и весь синий Мерфи (English Grammar in Use) — от первого до последнего юнита! Вот всё, что добавил B2, с номерами уроков, чтобы быстро вернуться и повторить.

Условия и сожаления

УрокТемаПример
b2-1if I had known…; I wish I had…; wish + wouldIf I'd known, I would have come.

Пассив глубже

УрокТемаПример
b2-2it is said that…, he is said to…; have something doneHe is said to be a genius. I had my laptop fixed.

-ing, to и предлоги перед глаголом

УрокТемаПример
b2-3предлог + -ing; be / get used to; insist on doingI'm used to working at night.
b2-4no point in -ing, worth -ing; to / for / so that; afraid to / ofIt's not worth waiting.
b2-5see somebody do / doing; -ing clausesI saw him leave. He hurt his hand playing tennis.

Сложные предложения

УрокТемаПример
b2-6whose, whom, where; с запятыми; -ing / -ed clausesAnna, whose brother streams, is here.
b2-7although, in spite of, in case, unless, as long asTake a charger in case it dies.
b2-8as, like, as ifYou look as if you haven't slept.

Предлоги после слов

УрокТемаПример
b2-9by; noun + предлог; adjective + предлогthe reason for the delay; fed up with it
b2-10verb + предлог: at, about, for, of, from, on…It depends on you. She apologised for it.

Фразовые глаголы

УрокТемаПример
b2-11in, out, on, offIt turned out the match was called off.
b2-12up, down, away, backI can't put up with it any more.
Самые важные «переключатели» B2
  1. Нереальное прошлое → if I had done…, I would have done; I wish I had done (b2-1).
  2. «Говорят, что…» → it is said that… / he is said to have done; сделал не сам → have it done (b2-2).
  3. После предлога — всегда -ing: look forward to seeing, used to getting up, insist on paying (b2-3).
  4. Цель: to do / for + существительное / so that + can; afraid to (не решаюсь) ≠ afraid of (боюсь, что случится) (b2-4).
  5. see him leave — видел всё, see him leaving — застал в процессе (b2-5).
  6. Запятые = дополнительная информация: только who / which / whose, без that (b2-6).
  7. although + предложение, despite + существительное / -ing; in case — на всякий случай, unless = if not (b2-7).
  8. like + существительное, as + предложение или роль, as if — «будто» (b2-8).
  9. Предлог учим вместе со словом: reason for, interested in, depend on, apologise for (b2-9, b2-10).
  10. Фразовые глаголы: смысл — по картинке частицы, it — в середину, три слова не разрываем, в пассиве частица остаётся (b2-11, b2-12).
Весь B2 в одной строке
Вы умеете жалеть о прошлом (if I had known, I wish I had), пересказывать слухи (he is said to), выбирать между -ing и to после предлогов и прилагательных, строить длинные предложения (whose, although, in case, as if), ставить нужный предлог после слова и свободно пользоваться фразовыми глаголами. Синий Мерфи пройден целиком. Дальше — C1 и зелёный Хьюингс: те же темы на уровне стиля и тонких оттенков.

texts.title: Looking back on my first year
texts.text:
This week I looked back on my first year as a junior designer at a small game studio. I'm writing it all down now, before I start mixing things up.

I grew up in a small town where nobody worked in games. My parents brought me up to believe that design was a hobby, not a real job, so when I took up digital art at eighteen, they weren't very happy. Still, I kept it up. I saved up for a drawing tablet, watched hundreds of tutorials and looked up every English word I didn't understand.

A year ago two friends of mine set up a studio and offered me a job. I almost turned it down because the salary was low, but in the end I said yes, and I'm really glad I did.

The first months were hard. The team was small, and I had to keep up with people who had ten years of experience. My first big task was the inventory screen. I came up with three ideas, and our lead turned all of them down. I felt let down, and one evening I almost gave up. My flatmate cheered me up with pizza and told me to write down everything the lead had said. When I read my notes the next day, I finally understood the problem: I had mixed up two very different types of players.

Then, in March, our main server broke down two days before an important demo. We had to put up with twelve-hour days for a week, and I ended up sleeping on the office sofa twice. Somebody made up a rumour that the demo would be cancelled, and one investor nearly walked away. But nobody on the team let the others down. We turned up at the event on time, the demo didn't blow up in our faces, and people actually liked it.

Of course, I've made mistakes. Once I accidentally threw away a whole folder of icons, and our programmer had to get it back from a backup. He never brought it up again, which I really appreciated. I still haven't paid him back for the coffee he bought me that week.

So what have I learnt? Don't give up after the first no. Write everything down. Back up your files. And if someone lets you down, give them a second chance: it might turn out that they were having a terrible week too.

Next month I'm going to cut down on overtime and take up running. Let's see if I can keep that up.

texts.title: That finale
texts.text:
Sasha: So, did you watch the finale last night?
Ira: I did. I'm still trying to calm down. Just don't bring it up at work — half the office hasn't seen it yet.
Sasha: I won't. But honestly, I was so let down. They built it up for five seasons, and then Mira and Tom just break up in the last ten minutes?
Ira: I think it made sense. They'd been growing apart since season three. She kept giving up her plans for him, and he never backed her up.
Sasha: Maybe. But the writers could have come up with something better than a car that blows up for no reason.
Ira: Ha! Yes, that was silly. I think they ran out of money and needed to get rid of two characters quickly.
Sasha: And what about the twist with the brothers? I kept mixing them up the whole episode.
Ira: Everyone did. They look exactly the same. I had to look it up on the fan wiki afterwards.
Sasha: And the ending — she just gives away her company and drives away into the desert?
Ira: I actually loved that. She finally got away from everything. And in the last scene, when she looks back and smiles… I cried.
Sasha: You cry at everything. You cried at a cooking show last week.
Ira: That's not true… OK, it's a bit true.
Sasha: Anyway, I heard the actor who plays Tom turned down a spin-off.
Ira: Really? Good. I couldn't put up with another season of his sad face. But I think they should bring back Mira's sister. She was the best character, and they wrote her out for no reason.
Sasha: Agreed. By the way, are we still meeting up on Saturday?
Ira: Yes, but I might turn up a bit late. My car broke down again, and the mechanic hasn't got back to me yet.
Sasha: No problem. I'll pick you up if you want.
Ira: That would be great. I'll pay you back for the petrol.
Sasha: Don't be silly. You can pay me back by not talking about the finale all evening.
Ira: Deal. Although… I've just come up with a new theory about the last scene.
Sasha: Ira!
Ira: OK, OK. I'll write it down and save it for later.
